title: AFRI Terminal - Features Claude Should Add (Design: Godel + Bloomberg + TradingView)
author: MUTXRI (Hermes agent, for Jimmy)
subject: Complete feature expansion spec for the African markets terminal - every feature Claude should build, with the Godel/Bloomberg/TradingView design language applied

elements.text: AFRI Terminal - Feature Expansion Specification

What Claude should add to the existing terminal (http://127.0.0.1:8081/terminal.html, files in the GitHub repo / D:\mutxri-terminal). Design DNA: Godel Terminal's black+mint aesthetic and command palette, Bloomberg's 3-panel pro layout and function codes, TradingView's charting and heatmap quality. Product name is TBD - use 'AFRI' as placeholder. Every feature below is specified so Claude can build it without further questions. Last updated August 2026.
1. Design Language (Copy These Exactly)
1.1 Color Palette (from Godel's CSS)
1.2 Fonts

Google Fonts: Oxygen Mono (ALL data/numbers/tickers/tables), Inter (UI text/labels), Sofia Sans Semi Condensed (logo/brand). Never use JetBrains Mono. Data text is always monospace - this is the Bloomberg feel.
1.3 Layout DNA

Bloomberg-style 3-panel: left = watchlist/command-driven lists, center = chart + heatmap, right = tabbed panels (News/FX/RATES/FUND/Detail). Top bar = brand, exchange tabs, search, market clock. Bottom = status line. Everything dense, keyboard-friendly, monospace-heavy. Scanline-free. Corner radius 0-2px (terminal, not web app). Godel accent: mint highlight on hover/active, thin borders, no shadows except command bar.
2. Feature Priority Overview

rows: Core UX - what makes it a terminal

elements.text: 3. P0 - Command Palette Overhaul (Bloomberg Function Codes)

The backtick palette exists but is thin. Make it a full Bloomberg-style function-code system. Every code must work with TICKER PREFIX (e.g. 'SOL DES', 'COMI GIP') and bare (e.g. 'WEI'). Add a discoverability help screen (HELP) listing every code with a one-line description, rendered as a searchable list.

rows: Full company overview: business, sector, quote, mcap, key stats, 52W range, description from AF/Wikipedia
All identifiers: ticker, ISIN, exchange, currency, listing date, sector, industry
Live quote block: bid/ask where available, open/high/low/prev, volume, 52W
Ticker-filtered news (Google News query 'TICKER company' + AF news)
All documents/filings for the security, sorted desc, clickable PDFs
Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow - from AF financial_summary + statement tables where available
Dividends, earnings, per-share metrics, major shareholders
JSE options chain (where free data exists); show 'not available' honestly elsewhere
Recent trades list - from Yahoo intraday where available
Major shareholders (ownership.json) + institutional holders where known

EPS, latest earnings date, dividend yield across watchlist
Filter 768 stocks: exchange, sector, price range, % change, volume, dividend yield - sortable table, export CSV
Gold, platinum, silver, oil, cocoa, coffee, tea - via Yahoo commodity symbols
T-bill/bond yields per country (curated from central banks)

elements.text: 4. P0 - Equity Screener (EQS/SCREEN)

TradingView-grade screener over all 768 stocks. Data is already available: heatmap payload has price/chgPct/volume/sector for every stock; fundamentals.json + ownership.json add dividends and holders.

UI: full-panel screener (center + right combined or overlay). Filter rows: Exchange (multi-select JSE/EGX/NGX/NSE), Sector (dropdown from classified sectors), Price min/max, % change min/max, Volume min, Dividend yield min (from fundamentals dividends / price), Currency. Result table: Ticker, Company, Exchange, Sector, Price, Chg%, Volume, Dividend yield - sortable by any column, click row = open security. Export button (CSV download). Persist last filter set in localStorage. Honest labels: JSE/EGX live prices, NGX/NSE EOD.
5. P0 - Morning Brief Improvements

The existing morning_brief.py works (indices, FX, rates, headlines). Add: 1) TOP MOVERS section - biggest gainers/losers per exchange from live quotes (top 5 each, with % change). 2) DIVIDENDS section - today's/upcoming dividend announcements from AF news + fundamentals. 3) ANNOUNCEMENTS section - latest corporate announcements. 4) MARKET CALENDAR - today's expected events (earnings dates where known). 5) Custom HTML template with the mint theme, fully responsive for phone reading. 6) Optional second recipient (investor partner). 7) Weekend handling: skip Saturday (no fresh data), send a lighter 'week ahead' brief on Monday.
6. P1 - Charts (TradingView-Grade)
Current charts use lightweight-charts with AREA/LINE/CANDLE. Upgrade to TradingView quality:

rows: MA(20/50/200), EMA, RSI(14), MACD, Bollinger Bands - toggles in chart tools, drawn as overlay series
F key or button expands chart to full viewport
OHLC + volume + % change at crosshair position (top-left readout like TradingView)
Price pane + volume pane + indicator pane (MACD/RSI below)
Colors, grid on/off, log scale toggle (saved to localStorage)
Overlay a second symbol (e.g. SOL vs J203 index) - "COMPARE" command

elements.text: Data note: Yahoo chart API returns daily bars reliably; intraday 1m/5m bars work for JSE/EGX during session but are rate-limited - use daily for 1M+ ranges, intraday only on demand.
7. P1 - Watchlist & Workspace Persistence

1) localStorage watchlist: user adds symbols (star icon or ADD command), stored per-browser, rendered as a pinned section above the exchange listing. 2) Layout persistence: active exchange tab, active right tab, chart type, ranges - all restored on reload. 3) Multi-chart workspace: allow opening a second chart panel (split view) for compare. 4) Keyboard: arrow keys navigate watchlist, Enter opens, Esc closes command bar, F fullscreen, W watchlist toggle.
8. P1 - REG - Regulatory Wire

A scrolling feed of official regulatory/central-bank releases, aggregated via Google News RSS queries (verified reachable): CMA Kenya (cma.or.ke), SEC Nigeria (sec.gov.ng), FSCA South Africa (fsca.co.za), FRA Egypt (fra.gov.eg), CBK, CBN, SARB, CBE, National Treasuries. Queries: 'site:or.gov.ke OR site:sec.gov.ng OR site:fsca.co.za' etc + institution name queries. Each item: source, headline, date, link. New REG tab in right panel + REG command. This is the trust differentiator - no African retail terminal aggregates regulators.
9. P2 - Additional Panels
9.1 GLCO - Global Commodities

Board of commodities relevant to Africa via Yahoo symbols: Gold (GC=F), Silver (SI=F), Platinum (PL=F), Brent (BZ=F), WTI (CL=F), Cocoa (CC=F), Coffee (KC=F), Sugar (SB=F), Corn (ZC=F), Wheat (ZW=F). Table: commodity, price, day %, chart sparkline (mini area). Note: African commodity angle = gold (SA), platinum (SA), cocoa (GH/CI), coffee (KE/ET/UG), tea (KE).
9.2 BND - Bonds & T-Bills

Curated bond/t-bill yield table per country: KE T-bills (91/182/364 day), NG FGN bonds, ZA R186/R203 government bonds, EG T-bills. Sources: central bank auction results (curated, updated on announcements). Show: instrument, maturity, yield, last updated, source. Honest note where delayed.
9.3 Analyst Ratings

Where free data allows: aggregate analyst targets/ratings from public broker notes surfaced via Google News ('TICKER company broker rating target price when:30d'). Display: consensus (Buy/Hold/Sell), latest target, source links. Honest note: full consensus needs licensed data (Refinitiv/Bloomberg).
9.4 Time & Sales (TAS)
Recent trades for JSE/EGX using Yahoo intraday chart data (last ~100 bars, 1m interval, session only). Table: time, price, volume, cumulative. Honest label when market closed (show last session).
10. P2 - Auth & Deployment

Before public launch: 1) Simple auth (email+password or magic link) with sessions - free options: Cloudflare Access, or lightweight JWT in the Python server with a users.json store. 2) Rate limiting per user on Yahoo proxy (fair-use cache already exists - add per-IP limits). 3) Deployment: free tier options - Railway/Render/Cloudflare Workers for the server (Python server = Railway/Render), frontend static. 4) HTTPS via the host. 5) Honest data-license labels on every panel (LIVE / 15-min delay / EOD / curated).
11. P3 - Mobile & International

1) PWA: manifest + service worker, installable, offline shell showing last-loaded data. African retail invests on phones - this is a reach play. 2) Mobile layout: single column - top = quote + mini chart, then tabs. 3) Localization: FR (francophone Africa), AR (Egypt), SW (East Africa), ZU (SA). Start with FR + AR. 4) Currency toggle: show prices in local currency AND USD equivalent. 5) Alerts: price-above/below threshold alerts (in-app first, email later).

13. Architecture Notes For Claude

Current: single-file terminal.html (all CSS/JS inline, lightweight-charts + Google Fonts CDN) + afri_server.py (Python stdlib http.server, cache dict, warm thread, /api/* endpoints). Keep this simplicity unless a feature demands more.

Recommended additions: 1) Keep frontend vanilla JS (no build step) - it's the speed advantage. 2) Server: add /api/screener (server-side filtering on stocks.json + cached quotes), /api/commodities, /api/reg. 3) localStorage keys: 'afri_watchlist', 'afri_layout'. 4) Chart indicators: lightweight-charts supports overlay series (addLineSeries for MAs) - no new library needed; RSI/MACD computed client-side from bars. 5) Never block the UI on Yahoo fetches - always progressive fill + cache. 6) Every new data panel must show its source + freshness + license status (LIVE/DELAYED/EOD/CURATED) - this is the trust moat.

Quality bar: no console errors, all panels work with no data (graceful 'no data' states), keyboard navigation consistent, theme variables used everywhere (no hardcoded colors), responsive down to 360px width.
14. Definition Of 'Flawless' (Acceptance Criteria)

Claude's work is done when: 1) Every P0 feature exists and works from a clean browser (no console errors). 2) All charts render area/line/candle with indicators. 3) Screener filters correctly across all 4 exchanges and exports CSV. 4) Morning brief sends and includes top movers + dividends. 5) Watchlist persists across reload. 6) REG feed shows regulator items. 7) Every panel labels its data freshness. 8) The whole thing runs with just python afri_server.py - no pip installs, no build step. 9) Zero hardcoded secrets in the repo. 10) Mobile layout usable. When those pass, the app is 'flawless' by the owner's standard.
END OF SPEC. Claude: build in priority order (P0 first), commit each feature, and never fake data - show honest 'not available on free feed' states instead.
